It is also the name of a wise and just king Ban, who ruled ancient Kiratarjuniya kingdom, stories of which are popular in the Purana chronicles. Banke is a name that evokes a sense of power, courage, and heroism, and has been immortalized in Hindu folklore, art, and literature.

The temple was established in the 17th century by Swami Haridas, a great devotee of Lord Krishna.

Another reference to the name Banke is found in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. Banasura, also known as Banasur or Banas, was a powerful demon king who was a great devotee of Lord Shiva. He was so devoted that Lord Shiva appeared before him and granted him a boon that no man could kill him. However, Banasura was later killed by Bhima, the strongest among the Pandava brothers, in a battle. The name Banasura or Banas can be considered a variant of Banke, as it is derived from the same Sanskrit root 'banas' meaning 'forest-dweller'.
